target_customer: Facebook advertisers and app marketers (Optilly); desktop software publishers and advertisers (InstallMonetizer)
problem: Optilly optimized Facebook ads by user attributes using multivariate testing and frequent bid changes; InstallMonetizer let free desktop-software developers earn per install from curated advertiser offers.
business_model: Ad optimization platform and a pay-per-install ad network (publishers paid per install)

founders.name: Vince Mundy
founders.background_notes: Told TechCrunch he was himself a desktop software developer facing the monetization problem.

founders.name: Lloyd Jacob
previous_startups: Several ad-tech and mar-tech companies, two exits, several failures (YC bio)
founders.background_notes: Mentor at SJSU Ideas Lab and YC Startup School 2019.

competitors.name: AdParlor
competitors.what: Facebook ads management and optimization platform with Ads API access
competitors.traction_then: Over one billion impressions per day on Facebook

technical_complexity.rationale: Ad-bid optimization through the Facebook Ads API and an installer ad network; standard engineering with some optimization logic.

defensibility.rationale: Publisher and advertiser two-sided network (9,000+ publishers claimed) but competing networks existed and platform access was controlled by Facebook.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not sourced; AdParlor was bought in 2011 and Facebook's own tools were growing.

market_need_then: InstallMonetizer reported 9,000+ publishers, installs doubling every two to three months and profitability (company claim, Jan 2013); Optilly's Facebook product is described in 2014 coverage.

branding.domain_note: optilly.com listed as the website; InstallMonetizer domain not sourced.

brand_strength.rationale: Only trade-press launch items; two product names under one company and no evidence of brand pull.

outcome_analysis: The cause of Optilly/InstallMonetizer's inactivity is not public: no shutdown post, acquisition or post-mortem was found. Known facts: YC W12, a $500K seed disclosed in January 2013 from a16z, SV Angel, Fenox and others, an installer ad network with 9,000+ publishers and a claimed profitable business, and a 2014 launch of an app-install marketing platform for Facebook. Any cause such as Facebook platform dependence is speculation.
notes: Round date is the TechCrunch article date; the raise date is not stated. Founded 2011 per YC, 2012 per CB Insights. Product history is unclear: YC says Facebook ad optimization, TechCrunch (2013) says desktop installer network, MediaPost (2014) says Optilly app-install platform for Facebook; order and any pivot not sourced. Shutdown date and cause not found. AdParlor, a Facebook-ads competitor, is dated Nov 2011; installer-network competitors are from the Jan 2013 article. Name origin not found. No Web Archive used.
